NICOMEDES MC. ABESAMIS HON. CATALINO R. CABRIGA Sangguniang Panlungsod Members Tayabas City Gentlemen: DILG OPINION NO. 153 2010 DEC 10 This has reference to your earlier letter addressed to Director Rolando M. Acosta, BLGS, this Department, where you both sought the Department's clarification on the following specific issues, to wit: "1) Do City Councilors Abesamis and Cabriga, as duly elected members of the Sangguniang Panlungsod of the City of Tayabas, deserve to receive just compensation as provided for by law, pending finality of the August 24, 2010 SC ruling? g) Who, what and how would Vice-mayor Rea be compelled to abide by the pertinent statutes, laws and issuances, specifically the afore-cited DILG Memorandum dated •24 September 2010?" In this regard, please be informed that on 18 November 2010, the Department was in receipt of the letter-reply dated 05 November 2010 of the Supreme Court informing the Department that their Resolution dated 24 August 2010 which granted the motions for reconsideration of the 21 December 2009 Decision and reinstated the 18 November 2008 declaring unconstitutional the Cityhood Laws, has not yet attained finality. Accordingly, the Department issued its recent Advisory dated 25 November 2010 reiterating our previous Advisory dated 24 September 2010 that absent a final judgment or order, there is no legal basis yet for the enforcement or execution of the Supreme Court Resolution dated 24 August 2010. Hence, all the local government units affected by the 24 August 2010 Resolution of the Supreme Court shall still be properly referred to as cities and the two (2) additional members in the Sangguniang Panlungsod may still validly discharge their duties and functions appurtenant to the position. A copy of the aforesaid recent Department Advisory dated 25 November 2010 is hereto attached for your ready perusal. On a final note, may we remind you that elective officials are bound by their oaths to uphold the law of the land as well as the rules issued by the duly constituted authorities in the country. The continued defiance of what is lawful and just may be an avenue for a possible administrative case of abuse of authority against the concerned elective official based upon Section 60 of the Local Government Code of 1991. We hope that we have addressed your concern accordingly. Very truly yours, ATTY. JESUS B.
